name: Spodumene mineral concentrate; beneficiation process; at plant; 5% lithium oxide
description:
This unit process produces a mineral concentrate from hard rock (spodumene) ores using mineral processing processes. The functional unit of the process is the production of 5% lithium oxide (Li2O) mineral concentrate that will be sent to a hydrometallurgical plant for further processing. The gate-to-gate system boundary starts with the input of a mill feed with 1.89% Li2O and ends with the production of a chemical concentrate with 5% Li2O. The process does not have co-products and all the environmental impacts are allocated to mineral concentrate production.

The input mill feed has 95% solids and solids have following composition by weight: LiO2:1.89%, Al2O3:16.0%, SiO2:73.3%, Fe2O3: 0.47%, Na2O: 2.36%, K2O: 2.78%, P2O5: 0.2%. The input mill feed undergoes numerous operations including crushing, dense media separation, grinding, desliming and mica and spodumene flotation circuits to produce a chemical concentrate . Most water requirements of the process are fulfilled with recycled water from the concentrate and tails thickeners and the process needs energy and chemicals for multiple operations. This process was modelled in excel to generate the mass and energy balances required to calculate the inventory.

processDocumentation.timeDescription: This process was designed based on state-of-art mineral concentrate production from spdodumene ore. The process parameters were collected based on industrial technical reports and scientific literature from 2018 to 2022.
processDocumentation.geographyDescription: This process converts input spodumene ore mill feed ( 1.89 %Li2O) to a mineral concentrate (5% Li2O) from typical Canadian lithium hard rock source, representitive of Canadian context. However, the process may be used in other regions in which the Li2O composition of spodumene ore mill feed and output mineral concentrate is similar.
processDocumentation.technologyDescription: The mill feed (1.89% LiO2) was crushed via jaw crusher to -12mm. It was then screened at 6mm and the oversized fraction was sent to Dense Media Separation (DMS) at a specific gravity of 2.65. DMS was used to remove the barren material resulting in a reduction of comminution energy required for flotation.  The sinks from DMS were added to the -6mm size fraction and ground using a ball mill at 80% solids to acheive P80 of around 200 microns. Products from the ball mill were sent to be deslimed. The slimes (overflow) <10 microns report to the tailings thickener. The underflow continued to the 2 step flotation circuit. The mica flotation circuit's goal is to remove mica from spodumene and to increase the LiO2 concentration to 2.51% LiO2. The mica flotation circuit consists of several mica rougher cells installed in series. The feed reported to the roughers and it's pH was maintained at 3 using sulphuric acid. Amine acetate was used as a collector, MIBC as the frother and a starch was used to depress spodumene during the float. The mica rougher float products reported to the tailings thickener while the remaining feed was sent to the spodumene flotation circuit after being deslimed again.  The spodumene flotation circuit is designed to produce a high grade spodumene chemical concentrate. The circuit consisted of several roughter flotation cells. The pH was controlled using NaOH, oleic acid was used as the collector for spodumene, and MIBC was used as a frother. The concentrate from flotation was sent to the concentrate thickener while the tailings were sent to the tails thickener. Please view the flow diagram below for additional information.
processDocumentation.inventoryMethodDescription: Attributional and gate to gate process.
processDocumentation.modelingConstantsDescription: To ensure the process model is simplistic in representing a generic lithium resource, the model assumed that Spodumene is the only Li-bearing minerals. In addition, aside from Lithium, the recovery of other potential by-products such as Cesium, Tantalium, Rubidium are not considered. This unit process for spodumene treatment is based off a 2,000 metric ton of lithium hydroxide monohydrate production plant scale.
processDocumentation.completenessDescription:
Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Technosphere flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. The mass balance for this process was calculated. The major elements that are simulated and followed in the model includes:  Li, Al, Fe, Si, K, Na, P.

Following elements/potential by-products are not modelled and hence are excluded from LCI
 - Cesium
 - Tantalium
 - Rubidium

The management/disposal of process tails, and the production and transport of chemicals and energy are excluded from gate-to-gate system boundary. It recommended to use appropriate background processes to calculate cradle-to-gate environmental impacts.


Elementary flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. Technosphere flows are cut-off at less than 1% based on environmental relevance. The mass balance for this process is calculated.
processDocumentation.dataSelectionDescription: The design criteria used to build the process simulation model for the Lithium Beneficiation Mill is based on information obtained from technical reports publically published on various Canadian lithium hard rock deposits. Supplementary information were also obtained from journal publications. When information cannot be sourced, provisional estimates and reasonable process assumptions were made. The source of the data used in the process model are clearly identified in the sources section. The process model is meant to represent a generic spodumene beneficiation mill to convert and produce lithium from a typical Canadian lithium hard rock source into a chemical concentrate for the hydromet plant.
processDocumentation.dataTreatmentDescription: Mass and energy balance data from process simulation model were converted per unit mass basis of 5% Li2O mineral concentrate produced. Electricity consumption data inludes all of the equipments at the mill and is reported as single aggregated value. Granular electricity data can be found in project publication (Kannangara et al. 2024).
processDocumentation.samplingDescription:
Boundary conditions: The gate-to-gate system boundary starts with the input of a mill feed with 1.89% Li2O and ends with the production of a chemical concentrate with 5% Li2O.
Data collection: Data were collected from industry sources and literature.
Uncertainty: Uncertainty was not evaluated for this process.
processDocumentation.useAdvice: This process was developed to be an input to lithium hydroxide monohydrate production.

sources.name: DRA Met-Chem (2018) Report on lithium mine

reviews.details: Mass and energy balances were done directly on Excel and reviewed. Process parameters and mill specifications were validated through expert opinion.

processDocumentation.intendedApplication:
SITUATION C1 -- ACCOUNTING The intended application for this process is for accounting purposes as described in Goal Situation C1 from the ILCD Handbook’s Detailed Guidance. LCA studies with this intended application offer "purely descriptive documentation of the system under analysis (e.g., a product, sector or country), without being interested in any potential consequences on other parts of the economy.” The studies categorized under Goal Situation C1 do consider existing benefits outside the analyzed system such as recycling.

The intended application is a purely descriptive accounting / documentation of the analysed system including existing interactions with other systems in the LCI model. The target audience of this model includes LCA practitioners, industry, and the general public.
